answer: Bind each identity to a one-time personhood credential from an outside registry, its commitment stored as a relic that cannot be reminted per clone. Weight requires enrollments dispersed across a plume of independent registries, so no captured issuer mints a farm. One real human per shell means N aliases need N distinct enrollments, super-linear and non-poolable, since cooperating operators cannot share a human. Each credential is a jetty binding the key to an institution beyond the farm, checkable at settlement from the committed proof. Failure mode: resale, bounded by revocation on reuse.
